pr_title: kubelet: Pods created and rapidly terminated get stuck
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug
/sig node

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This PR fixes the race when a pod gets terminated but crio has not had the chance to clean up the cgroup yet. The podKiller will register all pods into a map and bypass the cgroup cleanup in cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups if the kill is still pending.

In Openshift, we are seeing an issue where pods can be deleted from the API and the cgroup is torn down before the pod is completely killed. This is due to the Kubelet seeing the terminated pod from the API and the housekeeping routine (runs every 2 seconds) starts cleaning up the cgroup (cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups) if cgroupPerQOS is enabled.

The fix skips over the cgroup cleanup if the pod is being killed by podKiller. Once the pod exits the podKiller then `pcm.Destroy` is called within cleanupOrphanedPodCgroups.

- [x] Adds mock for FakeContainerManager
- [x] Adds mock for PodContainerManager
- [x] Unit test

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #98142

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: error reading container (probably exited) json message: EOF
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
Seeing this in the logs,
```
Jan 11 21:04:53.482614 ip-10-0-166-126 hyperkube[1733]: E0111 21:04:53.479356    1733 kuberuntime_sandbox.go:70] CreatePodSandbox for pod "pod-submit-status-0-0_e2e-pods-3370(c76833c3-6e57-4135-8968-2ed47a665cf8)" failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = error reading container (probably exited) json message: EOF                                                                                                                  
```

**What you expected to happen**:
Pods startup should not encounter EOF while reading any json (or any other file). 

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Observed while running this OpenShift test case,
https://github.com/openshift/origin/blob/e49fe16bd3eb5a177d04e59739bc91864d608d1c/vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/node/pods.go#L311

**Anything else we need to know?**:
It seems that we hit the race where the Pod attempts to start, and then Kubelet tears it down. There is a corresponding openshift bugzilla to track this issue, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1915085

comments:
/triage accepted
/priority important-soon

not sure if this merits critical-urgent

I think we're hitting the race condition as follows:

- Pod gets created
- Pod starts creating a sandbox
- Pod gets deleted, sandbox creation hasn't completed yet
- CreatePodSandbox fails

From what I can see, this is due to a flaw in `SyncPod`'s logic:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d70ee902fddc682863a3cc4f0d8eac0223ebf70b/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L666-L675

At any step in this sync loop, the pod could be deleted, but this code proceeds with the assumption that the underlying state as initially checked hasn't changed. So by the time we get to creating the sandbox, it might not even be necessary, and it can fail if the pod is deleted partway through:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d70ee902fddc682863a3cc4f0d8eac0223ebf70b/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L743-L755

 @rphillips suggested that we could pass in `PodManager` to lock critical state, but if we lock the pod for the duration of this sync loop, would there be performance implications? It's quite long.

edit: we could fix this by checking the `PodManager` after the sandbox creation is attempted by checking the state of the pod---if it's been killed, we could bail out.

That doesn't solve the overall issue with this code, it's more of a targeted hack, but does mostly address the problem.

Also, i don't see the `CreatePodSandbox for pod` in the community CI logs:
https://storage.googleapis.com/k8s-gubernator/triage/index.html?pr=1&text=CreatePodSandbox%20for%20pod

@dims for some background on what I believe is happening when this message comes up:
the `EOF` error comes from runc being killed. What it seems is happening is:
cri-o attempts to create the container, and is waiting on runc to finish.
kubelet gets the delete call, but sees the pod hasn't finished creating. Because it can't ask to RemovePodSandbox (it doesn't have an ID yet), it tears down the cgroup.
in tearing down the cgroup, systemd seems to SIGKILL runc. 

That output we're seeing is cri-o reporting that the runc process took too long, and is specific to cri-o. I wouldn't know what it would look like for containerd. Do y'all use systemd cgroup driver by default? that may also be part of it.

Ultimately, I believe this error really comes from the coordination between the kubelet sync loops:
When one goroutine is in the middle of creating a pod, another tears down the pod, and that is reported as an error. 
From my perspective, either the routines should be synchronized, or the error should be swallowed by kubelet.

/assign
so I can keep track of this
